canonical_topic: Mineral rights ownership and licensing for E&P
definition: Energy companies lease land to extract fuel and compensate both the surface land owner and the mineral rights owner (often the same or different parties) via royalties, a share of production profit; who owns subsurface mineral rights varies by country.
core_idea: In the U.S., subsurface fossil fuel rights are commonly privately owned, whereas in most other countries they belong to the government; regardless of ownership, exploration companies must obtain licenses first to explore and then, separately, to develop identified resources for production.
key_points: Producers pay royalties — a percentage of production profit — to land and mineral rights owners.
U.S.: subsurface fossil fuel rights are often privately owned.
Most other countries: subsurface resources are government-owned.
Two licensing stages: one to explore for new resources, a separate one to develop/produce once resources are identified.
relationships: Royalty-based compensation connects to the Tax and Royalty contract structure described later in the same section.
caveats: Ownership of surface land does not automatically imply ownership of subsurface mineral rights, and the two can be held by different parties.
